title: [Demo] Linux Terminal Basics
description: Essential commands and concepts for navigating the Linux command line.

questions.text: Which command is used to list directory contents including hidden files in Linux?
questions.explanation: In Linux, the "-a" (all) flag for "ls" reveals hidden files whose names start with a dot.

questions.text: What does the "pwd" command stand for and do?

options.text: Print Working Directory: displays current full pathname
Process Wait Daemon: inspects background processes
Path Where Destination: finds installed binary paths

questions.explanation: "pwd" stands for Print Working Directory and prints the absolute path of the current directory.

questions.text: Which command redirects the standard output of one command as input to another command?
questions.explanation: The pipe operator "|" connects the stdout of the left command to the stdin of the right command.

questions.text: Which permission octal value grants read, write, and execute permissions to the owner, and read-only to others and group?
questions.explanation: rwx = 4+2+1 = 7 (owner), r-- = 4 (group), r-- = 4 (others), giving 744. (755 would grant execute to group/others).

questions.text: Which signal number corresponds to SIGKILL, which cannot be caught or ignored?
questions.explanation: SIGKILL (kill -9) immediately terminates a process without giving it an opportunity to clean up.

questions.text: Which command searches for patterns of text within files using regular expressions?
questions.explanation: grep (Global Regular Expression Print) searches plain-text data sets for lines matching a pattern.
